title: Volley Supervisor Effective Config
description: Retained effective global supervisor config published to volley/_waves/_config. See spec section 4.6.4. The tunable model lives in $defs/tunables (every key optional, every key bounded, no other keys) so a wave file's config: overrides and a config_set patch can reference it; the retained topic requires every tunable to be present.

version.description: Monotonic; bumped on every applied change.

tunables.description: Every runtime-tunable supervisor setting, all keys optional, no other keys. Reference this from overrides (a wave file's config: block, wave-state effective_config, a config_set patch).

tunableProperties.description: The tunable keys and their bounds, left open so the retained payload can add its metadata fields (version, updated_at, updated_by). Consumers other than the retained payload use the closed $defs/tunables.

hard_ceiling.description: Runaway fuse: maximum concurrently live supervised agents across all waves.

spawn_budget_multiplier.description: Raises a wave's derived spawn budget (every task's pipeline roles plus retry headroom) to multiplier x task count when that is more. Counts retries and reviewers; spawn_budget in the wave file overrides both.

lease_pools.description: Heavy-operation lease pools, keyed by pool name (topic-segment grammar).

memory_pressure_max_level.description: Highest OS memory-pressure level (1 normal, 2 warn, 4 critical) at which spawns are still admitted.

heartbeat_alarm_s.description: Seconds without a hook heartbeat (while working and alive, no tool call in flight) before the screen is read; a screen still changing across two such windows opens a hooks_silent alarm.

idle_grace_s.description: Seconds an agent may sit idle (its turn ended, no terminal status) before it is nudged once; still idle another grace later opens an agent_stalled decision.

background_wait_max_s.description: Seconds, counted from the start of the idle, that evidence of an idle agent's own work (background_wait, a lease, running shells, a fresh worktree write) holds off the idle nudge; past it the nudge path resumes.

stall_backoff_max_s.description: Cap on the gap before a re-opened agent_stalled decision: the n-th re-open waits idle_grace_s × 2^n after the answer, at most this long.

blocked_undecided_stall_ms.description: Milliseconds an agent whose retained status is blocked may go with no decision naming it (open, or answered for that status) before it is stalled (an agent_stalled decision: respawn | stop task). Optional in the retained payload: a supervisor that predates it omits it.

tool_in_flight_max_s.description: Seconds a tool call in flight (its PreToolUse boundary seen, its PostToolUse not yet) holds off the silence probe; past it, a screen static for heartbeat_alarm_s falls back to the screen_static path.

mailbox_wake_after_ms.description: Milliseconds the supervisor waits for an agent's hooks to ack a mailbox message it sent (a steer, a nudge, an answer) before it types the fixed wake line into the agent's session; only an agent idle at its prompt is woken, once per message.

fallback_model.description: Model offered in a model_switch decision on credit exhaustion; null disables the offer.

session_expiry_s.description: MQTT v5 session expiry for persistent mailbox sessions (new connections only).

worktree_root.description: Directory under which the supervisor creates agent worktrees (applies to later spawns).

spawn_timeout_s.description: Seconds to wait for a spawned agent's registration before retrying.

spawn_retry_max_s.description: Cap, in seconds, on the automatic retry delay of a failed spawn (the delay starts at 30 s and doubles per failure).

spawn_retry_max.description: Failed spawn attempts in a row after which the supervisor stops retrying automatically (its spawn_failed decision then says so).

brief_preface_max_bytes.description: Largest brief preface (spec section 4.6.9) the supervisor accepts, in bytes; a larger one refuses the wave (BRIEF_PREFACE_TOO_LARGE). Optional in the retained payload: a supervisor that predates it omits it.

wake_grace_s.description: Seconds after a detected host sleep/wake during which liveness alarms are held and reaped statuses are re-verified: a reap is accepted only if no heartbeat arrives within it.

screen_tail_interval_s.description: Seconds between captures of each live agent's terminal for its retained screen topic (spec section 4.6.6).

tmux_cols.description: Columns of a paired machine's tmux session at launch, and when the Desk's Terminal popout closes (spec section 4.6.4).

tmux_rows.description: Rows of a paired machine's tmux session at launch, and when the Desk's Terminal popout closes (spec section 4.6.4).

stop_grace_s.description: Seconds a stopped wave's agents get to publish a terminal status after their cancel; any still running then is force-retired (records cleared, login deleted).

dynsec_batch_ms.description: Milliseconds the supervisor collects broker login changes (mints, deletes) before sending them as one Dynamic Security control message, so the broker rewrites its state file once per batch (spec section 4.6.13). Optional in the retained payload: a supervisor that predates it omits it.

credential_sweep_interval_s.description: Seconds between credential sweeps, which delete the broker logins of agents that are no longer live (spec section 4.6.13). Optional in the retained payload: a supervisor that predates it omits it.

claude.description: Claude account profiles (spec section 4.6.11). Optional in the retained payload: a supervisor that predates them omits it.

default_account.description: The Claude account an agent runs under when neither its task nor its wave names one. null (the default): balance across the machine's signed-in accounts, spending the room that expires first in the 5-hour, 7-day and the model family's weekly windows (spec section 4.6.12); a one-login machine uses its login; most_headroom (a legacy name) means the same; primary or a registry id pins.

warn_at_pct.description: When an account's 5-hour window reaches this used percentage, the supervisor opens an account_limit decision for each wave with agents on it (spec section 4.6.12). It never moves a wave on its own.

balance.description: The balancing rule (spec section 4.6.12): which signed-in account an automatic pick takes. Read from the supervisor's config; a wave's own override does not apply (the rank has no wave). Optional in the retained payload: a supervisor that predates it omits it.

cap_pct.description: An account is eligible for the automatic pick only while every window it reported is under this used percentage (spec section 4.6.12). When every candidate is at or over it, the least over is still picked; it never refuses a spawn.

tie_band_pct.description: Accounts whose pace scores are within this percentage of the band's leader count as equal and go to the one with fewer agents (spec section 4.6.12).

branch_update.description: How the pipeline's rebase step brings a PR branch up to date when the release branch moved (spec section 4.6.4): rebase (rebase onto the release branch, then a lease-guarded force-push) or merge (merge the release branch in, then a normal push: no force-push of any kind; the new head must descend from the old one). Optional in the retained payload: a supervisor that predates it omits it.

agent_mcp.description: The MCP servers a launched agent loads (spec section 4.6.4): strict (only the supervisor's own volley server: a reproducible, minimal agent) or inherit (the user's own servers too, such as plugin servers and connectors, beside the supervisor's volley server, which takes over a user-scope server of the same name). Optional in the retained payload: a supervisor that predates it omits it.

agent_mcp_allow.description: Under agent_mcp: inherit, the user's MCP servers a launched agent loads, by name (spec section 4.6.4): the supervisor copies each named entry from the profile's ~/.claude.json (user and local scope) and the repository's .mcp.json into the agent's own MCP config and launches it strict, so only those start. Empty: every server, as inherit alone. A name found nowhere, unapproved in .mcp.json or of an entry shape volleyd does not copy is skipped and journaled once per wave and machine. Optional in the retained payload: a supervisor that predates it omits it.

agent_auto_compact_pct.description: The share of a launched agent's context window at which Claude Code compacts its conversation (spec section 4.6.4): the supervisor exports CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW = this percentage of the model's window, in tokens, clamped to Claude Code's 100000..1000000. 0: the variable is not set and Claude Code's own default applies. Optional in the retained payload: a supervisor that predates it omits it.

public_hygiene.description: What a supervisor's reviewers flag as public hygiene (spec section 4.6.8): auto (read the repository's visibility once per wave version; a public repository, or one whose visibility could not be read, gets the P1 check, a private or internal one a non-blocking P3 note), on (always the P1 check) or off (no hygiene check). Optional in the retained payload: a supervisor that predates it omits it.

hosts.description: Remote hosts a wave task may name with host: <name>: agents run in tmux on another machine over SSH, reaching the broker through a reverse tunnel. A wave file's inline host: { type: ssh, ... } is layered over the entry it names. A host's name is never local or auto, which host: reserves; a paired machine's entry is added by peer_join (spec section 4.6.14).

repos.description: Repositories by their canonical GitHub owner/name, compared case-insensitively, and the machines holding a clone of each (spec section 4.6.4): machines all (every machine, the supervisor's own included) or a list of machine names (hosts.<name> keys or the supervisor's fleet.local_name). A listed machine's clone is its hosts.<name>.repos entry when it has one, else the managed clone at <fleet.repo_root>/<owner>/<name>. Optional in the retained payload: a supervisor that predates it omits it.

require_fresh_base.description: Before cutting an agent's worktree on any host, the supervisor fetches the release branch there; true: a fetch that fails fails the spawn, so no agent starts on a stale base (spec section 4.6.15). false: the host's last fetched copy is used. Optional in the retained payload: a supervisor that predates it omits it.

retire_close_session.description: true: retiring an agent also ends its session (its workspace closed, its claude process stopped on the supervisor's own machine), journaled agent_session_closed (spec section 4.6.4). false: finished sessions stay open for inspection. Optional in the retained payload: a supervisor that predates it omits it.

placement.description: Automatic placement across machines (spec section 4.6.15), for waves with placement: auto and tasks with host: auto. Optional in the retained payload: a supervisor that predates it omits it.

load_per_core_max.description: A machine whose load per core (the higher of its 1- and 5-minute load averages) is above this takes no new placement.

mem_available_min_pct.description: A machine with less available memory, in percent, takes no new placement.

disk_free_min_gb.description: A machine with less free disk, in GB, where its worktrees live takes no new placement.

down_decision_after_s.description: Seconds a machine with unfinished tasks may stay down before the supervisor opens a machine_down decision. It never re-places a task without an answer.

weights.description: Relative weights of each kind of headroom in a candidate's score, renormalised over the headrooms that are known (spec section 4.6.15). They need not sum to 100, but not all four may be 0.

cpu.description: Weight of CPU headroom (1-minute load per core).

slots.description: Weight of free agent slots (max_agents minus placed).

nudge_on_merge.description: When a wave's PR merges, send one steering message to its running implementers: files (those whose task's files overlap the merged PR's), all, or off.

default.description: The placement of a wave file without placement: (spec section 4.6.15). auto places its unpinned tasks across machines once a paired machine (a hosts.<name> entry) is configured; with none, or under local, they run on the supervisor's own machine.

archive_ended_after_h.description: Hours after its wave_stopped or wave_complete that the supervisor archives an ended wave (spec section 4.6.20); 0: never. Optional in the retained payload: a supervisor that predates it omits it.

archive_on_ack.description: true: a complete wave is archived as soon as its wave_complete decision is answered (spec section 4.6.20). Optional in the retained payload: a supervisor that predates it omits it.

ci_rate_limit_backoff_ms.description: After a rate-limited GitHub answer (HTTP 403 or 429), the supervisor makes none of that wave's CI calls for this long (longer when the answer's output names a Retry-After). Optional in the retained payload: a supervisor that predates it omits it.

fleet.description: The supervisor's own machine as a placement candidate (spec section 4.6.15). Optional in the retained payload: a supervisor that predates it omits it.

local_name.description: The name the supervisor's own machine record is published under (volley/_system/machines/<name>); null: derived from the machine's host name (spec section 4.6.15). Never a hosts.<name> key. The retained effective config carries the resolved name, never null.

local_agents.description: How the supervisor's own machine takes auto-placed tasks (spec section 4.6.15). always: a candidate like any peer. fallback: only while no paired machine is eligible, under fleet.fallback. never: not a candidate (a task pinned to local still runs there). null: fallback when any hosts.<name> is configured, else always; the retained effective config carries the resolved value. A value chosen in the Desk is set explicitly; volleyd config set fleet.local_agents null derives it again.

local_terminal.description: The terminal agents on the supervisor's own machine run in (spec section 4.6.15): cmux workspaces or detached tmux sessions named volley-<wave>-<task>-<role>. null: cmux on macOS when cmux is installed, else tmux. volley setup's Terminal step records its choice here. Read when the supervisor starts: a change applies at its next start.

fallback.description: The profile the supervisor's own machine runs under while it is the fallback (local_agents: fallback, no paired machine eligible; spec section 4.6.15).

max_agents.description: Under local_agents: fallback, the most supervised agents the supervisor's own machine runs while it is the fallback; hard_ceiling still caps the total.

per_machine.description: Per heavy pool, the leases holders on the supervisor's own machine may hold while it is the fallback; a pool not named here gets 1 when it has a per-machine cap there (per_machine or a per_machine_overrides entry). 0 keeps heavy tasks off it. The Desk offers a row for each pool that sets per_machine; name any other pool in config.yaml.

repo_root.description: Where managed clones live on every machine: a repository owner/name assigned to a machine (repos.<owner/name>.machines) is cloned at <repo_root>/<owner>/<name> there, a leading ~ being that machine's home (spec section 4.6.4). An adopted clone (hosts.<name>.repos) keeps its own path.

autopilot.description: Decisions the supervisor answers itself from its policy table, and its remediation budgets (spec section 4.6.16), and who merges a gated PR (spec section 4.6.17). Each maximum counts automatic answers per wave under one budget key. Optional in the retained payload: a supervisor that predates it omits it.

enabled.description: false: every decision waits for the owner, as before autopilot; takes effect at the next decision.

owner_only.description: Decision kinds the supervisor never answers itself: it escalates them to the owner (owner_only).

relaunch_max.description: Automatic relaunches of one task's role after a bad launch (hooks_auth_failed, mcp_not_registered, unknown_screen).

nudge_max.description: Automatic extra nudges of one stalled run (agent_stalled).

respawn_max.description: Automatic respawns of one task's role (agent_blocked, agent_stalled).

rereview_max.description: Automatic re-reviews of one task (pr_head_moved, a stale review at the gate).

ci_fixup_max.description: Automatic CI fixups of one task (ci_failed on the change's own head answered fixup).

question_max.description: Agent questions answered automatically for one run (agent_question).

account_move_max.description: Automatic account moves of one task's role (agent_account_limit).

budget_raise_max.description: spawn_budget_exhausted: automatic raise by <n> answers may take the wave's spawn budget up to this multiple of its derived budget.

inbox_answered_ttl_s.description: How long an answered needs-you inbox item stays retained with its answered record before the supervisor clears it (spec section 4.6.18).

merge.description: Who merges a gated PR when the wave file has no merge: key: auto (the supervisor squash-merges exactly the gated head, journaled merged_by_supervisor) or manual (a human merges; the supervisor only observes the merge).

merge_retry_max.description: Merges GitHub may refuse at one gated head (the head moved, checks required, branch protection) before the supervisor opens a merge_refused decision.

merge_transient_backoff_s.description: The waits in seconds before each retry of a merge the host refused transiently at one gated head (busy, a 5xx, a rate limit, a dropped connection); attempt n waits entry n. Such refusals never count toward merge_retry_max; one more past the last entry opens the merge_refused decision.

merge_transient_retry_max.description: Automatic retry answers to a merge_refused decision whose transient backoff ladder was spent, per task (policy row merge_refused/transient).

delete_branch.description: Autopilot merges also delete the PR's head branch (gh pr merge --delete-branch).

reconnect_grace_s.description: How long a wave whose owner is a coordinator name shows coordinator.state reconnecting after the agent bound to the name went away (terminal status or LWT) with no other agent binding to it; then gone.

incident_wait_max_s.description: How long a red head classified as an infra incident (an infra-shaped run, or GitHub's status page reporting an Actions or API incident) is held in CI and re-checked every poll before the supervisor opens its ci_failed decision, escalated budget_exhausted.

fix_flake_max.description: Flake fixers (synthetic fix-<slug> tasks, one per distinct failing test) the supervisor adds to one wave; a fix_flake request past it escalates the blocked task's ci_failed decision budget_exhausted.

digest_min_interval_s.description: The shortest gap between two digests of one wave with the same trigger (spec section 4.6.16): a second escalation inside it publishes no new digest and sends no push.

merge_train.description: The merge queue gates and merges up to four gated PRs as one train; false: one PR at a time.

max_agents.description: The most supervised agents this host runs at once (spec section 4.6.15); hard_ceiling still caps the total. Derived at join from the machine's size, min(floor(cores / 3), floor(memory_total_mb / 4096)) clamped to 2..16; unset, it is derived the same way from the machine record, and 4 when the size is unknown. An explicit value always wins.

drain.description: true: the host takes no new placements and its running agents finish (spec section 4.6.15).

repos.description: Adopted clones on this machine: a repository owner/name to its clone's absolute path there, used in place of the managed path under fleet.repo_root (spec section 4.6.4). Its worktrees are still created under the repository's managed worktree root, unless worktree_root is set.

remoteHostProperties.description: The settings of one SSH + tmux host, left open so the wave file's inline host can add type and name. Paths are on the remote machine and must be absolute. Object keywords only (no type), so the wave file can apply it to a string-or-object host.

target.description: ssh destination, [user@]host (an ssh config alias works). Never starts with '-', so it can never be read as an option.

repo.description: Deprecated: hosts.<name>.repos. The wave repository's clone on the remote machine; the release branch is fetched into it before each worktree is cut. Still accepted; once the machine's record reports the clone's origin, the supervisor migrates it to repos.<owner/name>.machines and hosts.<name>.repos.<owner/name> (spec section 4.6.4).

worktree_root.description: Directory on the remote machine under which agent worktrees are created (default: .volley-worktrees beside repo).

volley_dir.description: The volley checkout on the remote machine; its packages/volley-hooks is the agents' VOLLEY_HOOKS_DIR.

remote_port.description: Port on the remote machine's 127.0.0.1 that reaches the broker; agents get broker_url mqtt://127.0.0.1:<remote_port>. Not 1883 by default: a remote machine running its own broker has that port taken.

supervise.description: true: the supervisor keeps ssh -N -R <remote_port>:<broker> up itself (one per target and remote_port). false: the tunnel is operator-managed and only checked.

per_machine.description: The most leases of this pool that holders on one machine may hold at once, at most capacity (spec section 4.6.5). Unset: capacity.

per_machine_overrides.description: Per machine name (a hosts.<name> key, the supervisor's fleet.local_name, or local), the most leases of this pool its holders may hold, in place of per_machine; at most capacity (checked by the supervisor). 0: none on that machine (spec section 4.6.5).

match.description: Regular expressions matched against each command the shell would execute (not comments, heredocs or message text); a match requires a lease from this pool.

perMachineWithinCapacity.description: per_machine is at most capacity: one implication per capacity value below the bound (JSON Schema cannot compare two values).
